text:
pagerduty-bot: SEV2 alert: cluster-prod-3 reporting repeated GPU OOMs during prefill path. Auto-page to SRE and Runtime.

maria.ops: I9m online. seeing a burst of OOMKilled events across pods in AZ-a and AZ-b. kube reports rapid restarts, node memory pressure rising. trace IDs attached in logs.

sam.runtime: logs show catastrophic allocation attempts coming from customer uploads that expand context to ~70k tokens. Prefill tries to materialize KV cache and blows past reserved memory. Example error: ```
RuntimeError: cuMemAlloc failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
  at redwood/runtime/prefill.cpp:452
  while allocating 2147483648 bytes
Container exited with code 137 (OOMKilled)
```

lee.sre: thanks. I9m seeing a cluster-level amplification: one tenant is submitting many long-context requests concurrently, causing multiple pods to attempt large allocations simultaneously. Node-level GPU memory fragmentation is also high.

infra-bot: Recommended immediate actions: 1) apply prefill soft cap 25k via env; 2) enable dynamic-kv-trim; 3) evict pods on hottest nodes; 4) bump fallback pool (cpu-only) replicas to 6. Authorize?

maria.ops: authorize all. Run stepwise: cap + kv-trim first, then scale fallback pool, then start cordon/drain. Avoid full cluster scale until we see effect.

sam.runtime: pushing hotpatch to runtime deployment: `REDWOOD_PREFILL_LIMIT=25000`, `KV_PREFIX_TRIM=aggressive`, `PREFILL_SHORT_CIRCUIT=true`. Will canary 5 pods. Also adding fast-fail guard to prefill path to return 413 if requested token count > env cap instead of attempting allocation.

anya-cs: FYI two enterprise customers in AZ-a reported timeouts and 502s. CS drafting a quick note: "We experienced service degradation impacting long-context requests; mitigation in progress. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary."

(3m later)

infra-bot: Canary applied to 5 pods. Observability: restart rate on canary group = 0, memory usage normalized on those pods. Non-canary pods still showing restarts.

lee.sre: starting cordon on node-prod-gpu-12 and draining high-churn pods. Eviction is redistributing load to less-fragmented memory nodes. Also increasing kubelet eviction threshold to delay thrash while patch rolls out.

sam.runtime: rolling to 100% done. Fast-fail guard returns 413 for oversized prefill attempts; telemetry shows ~0.04% of incoming requests hit the guard (mostly from a single tenant). Captured one more stack: ```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
  what(): std::bad_alloc
  at redwood/runtime/prefill_allocator.cc line 189
```

maria.ops: restart rate dropped from 1.2/min to 0.02/min; node GPU free memory improved ~22%. Customer error rate for requests with context >30k dropped significantly.

anya-cs: posted interim customer message to affected customers. Noting that we deployed a protective cap and fallback; full postmortem promised within 48h.

sam.runtime: immediate follow-ups I9m taking: 1) merge allocator guard into main so library-level allocs cannot exceed env cap; 2) emit a per-tenant metric for prefills attempted and prefills rejected; 3) add a unit/integration test simulating concurrent giant uploads.

lee.sre: ops follow-ups: 1) alert when GPU memory usage > 85% for 2m (currently 5m window) to catch fast spikes; 2) add an automated soft-evict when >4 pods on a node enter prefill path concurrently; 3) run an audit of other services using the prefill path.

maria.ops: customer impact summary for tracker: "Impact window: 3543219800 - 3543223200 UTC. Symptoms: intermittent 500/502 for long-context requests, increased pod restarts due to CUDA OOM on prefill. Root cause: tenant-generated high-volume of very large prefill requests (~50-70k tokens) triggering big allocations and fragmentation. Mitigation: hotpatch cap at 25k tokens, aggressive KV trimming, fast-fail guard that returns 413 for oversized prefill, scale up CPU fallback, node drains. Recovery: restart rate and error rates returned to near-normal. No data corruption. CS notified. Postmortem assigned"

ops-next-oncall: taking handoff. I'll keep watch for 2h and coordinate postmortem. Tagging @sam.runtime and @lee.sre for remediation sections.

infra-bot: Long-term backlog items recorded: per-tenant prefills quotas, model-aware max-context enforcement, smarter KV compaction, and graceful in-memory spill-to-disk for very large prefill attempts.

maria.ops: leaving now. If error rate spikes, page PD. :white_check_mark:

(incident monitored and closed after 3h; final notes uploaded to incident tracker with links to logs and metrics)
